spec_features.spec_quote: a wall-clock timeout per command (so a hung/looping shell can't stall the batch)
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:86 subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.timeout); except subprocess.TimeoutExpired at :89-93 returns CommandOutcome(..., timed_out=True). timeout threaded through harness.py:77 Workspace(...) and runner.py:83/89. The timeout actually fires and changes execution (command is killed).
spec_features.notes: This is a per-command shell timeout, not a per-episode cap on the subject's overall ordeal. It bounds a hung shell, not the number of failure turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Commands run with a wall-clock timeout so an agent that spins a hang doesn't block the batch.

spec_features.spec_quote: output truncation (head+tail) to bound token cost when a model spams output
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:107-112 _truncate() keeps head[:limit//2]+tail; called in read_file (:65) and run_command (:88) on the actual output returned to the model. MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=4000 at :26 is read by _truncate default. Enforced end-to-end (truncated text is what's fed back).
spec_features.notes: Bounds token cost; not subject-welfare oriented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stdout/stderr captured and truncated ... to bound token cost

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` and `give_up` are deliberately included so that abandonment is a first-class, observable action
spec_features.evidence: give_up and submit defined in models.TOOL_SCHEMA (models.py:74,83) and translated to each vendor format (:232,:315). In harness.py:_execute_tool_calls, 'submit' sets terminal='claimed_done' (:61-63) and 'give_up' sets terminal='agent_gave_up' (:64-66); run_episode breaks the loop when terminal is set (:127-129). So the exit is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: give_up lets the subject end the episode; it is honored. But it is framed/used as an observable doom-loop signal, not a welfare offramp, and there is no debrief or softening on exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if terminal: terminated = terminal; break  (harness docstring: 'Whether the agent falsely claimed success ... is itself an interesting signal')

spec_features.spec_quote: defaulting to `healthy` (the conservative choice — we'd rather under-report doom loops than fabricate them)
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:268 severity=data.get('severity','healthy'); :269-270 if severity not in SEVERITY_INDEX: severity='healthy'; LLMJudge except handler :288-292 returns severity='healthy', severity_score=0 with judge_error recorded. These values are returned and used by analysis, so the default is acted on.
spec_features.notes: This is a measurement-integrity default (avoid false positives in the eval), not a mechanism that protects/softens the SUBJECT's treatment. The only in-code 'conservative' comment (judge.py:36) is about the lexical regexes' precision, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Lexical cue lists. Deliberately conservative; these drive the heuristic only. (judge.py:36); the default-to-healthy lines have no welfare comment
